item.title: Lights out, Instagram off? The changes to Meta for teens could be a big deal
item.description: Researchers and advocates are applauding the changes that Meta agreed to make for minors on Instagram and Facebook. Cutting kids off at night and during the school day are two big changes.

item.title: Trump cuts to science advisory boards have long-lasting consequences, researchers say
item.description: The federal government recruits top experts to volunteer to advise on pressing research issues of the day. Since President Trump took office, hundreds of these experts have been dismissed.

item.title: How America celebrated and mourned Dolly Parton, in Nashville and beyond
item.description:
The great Dolly Parton died earlier this week and tributes have poured in from across the country.

Fans are mourning the loss of a country music icon who not only changed the musical landscape but gave back to communities with her Imagination Library program and donations to develop the Moderna COVID vaccine.

item.title: Why is one WNBA team calling in national security experts?
item.description: The WNBA's popularity has risen in recent years, but so have threats and abuse directed at its players. One team is taking a novel approach to this, by partnering with national security specialists.

item.title: Sae Joon Park, a Purple Heart veteran who self-deported, receives pardon
item.description: His removal order was triggered by two convictions from over 15 years ago, when he struggled with untreated PTSD. New York's governor said Park earned a "second chance through rehabilitation."

item.title: Fed's Kevin Warsh warns inflation is too high, sparking bets rate hikes are coming
item.description: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated his commitment to fighting inflation in a major speech — raising expectations that rate hikes may be coming, though he did not clearly spell out a path going forward.

item.title: New Jersey is a fossil hotspot, with answers about the day the dinosaurs died
item.description: Paleontologist Ken Lacovara never expected to find critical fossil data in a New Jersey suburb—let alone info about the asteroid that killed the dinosaurs. His dig site is now a fossil park and museum.

item.title: Experts warn more flooding might hit Nepal. And, Fed chairman to give key address
